candidates.comment: The speaker Lewis Loflin began by explaining how the common problem of connecting MOSFETs in parallel lies in the oftentimes neglected Cgs, or capacitance gate source, which is also connected in parallel when MOSFETs are connected in parallel. As a result, the capacitance adds up as capacitors in parallel do. In turn, the increased capacitance disrupts the drive signal. Additionally, with enhancement mode MOSFETs, they are always off until the gate action turns them on. Turning the I/O pin to MOSFETs on and off will result in a charge and discharge curve in the output voltage waveform, which ultimately causes the unexpected circuit behavior many witness in experiments.
